speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: asked the Minister for Education whether there are any plans to introduce cybersecurity awareness as part of the core curriculum in Primary schools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: MOE recognises the importance of equipping students to use technology safely and responsibly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: These lessons are supported by digital literacy resources, covering cybersecurity-related topics such as safeguarding personal information when using the Internet and social media, and hosted on the Student Learning Space (SLS) online platform.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Beyond the formal curriculum, the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA) supports the Ministry of Education's (MOE) efforts by providing assembly talks and other enrichment programmes in schools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: MOE will continue to ensure that students are equipped with cybersecurity knowledge and skills to use technology safely and responsibly in their day-to-day lives.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: As she has said, we all agree that technology is very important in going forward.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: We also agree that the earlier the introduction is done, the better.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I am glad to know about the programmes that already exist to introduce cybersecurity.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: But, with respect to both cybersecurity and coding, which we have also discussed in previous Parliamentary Questions (PQs), it is really important that our children are given that digital mindset early in life; otherwise, it could be another source of future inequality and lack of social mobility.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Because I have seen great discrepancies in children who have resources and can code in all kinds of languages as kids, versus those who do not even have a computer when they come in.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I also think that introducing coding and cybersecurity in the core curriculum is very important to inspire kids to learn about these careers early in their life which foundational computational skills like Math and Science may not actually introduce them to.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This is also something that MOE agrees with and that is why a lot of our learning resources are hosted on student learning spaces.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And as I mentioned in my response earlier, cybersecurity awareness, cyber wellness are a very integral part of our CCE curriculum, which is available to all Primary school students and above, such as, Secondary schools and IHLs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, we want to introduce cyber wellness, cyber awareness, cybersecurity as early as possible, but we also recognise that we have to make the information available in an age-appropriate manner so that the students are best able to absorb the information and also know how to interact with the online space responsibly.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: Can I call for it again to be in the core curriculum?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: If you look at countries like Korea, for example, they have in the core curriculum dealing with robots.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: So, all those sorts of things are just going to be very important going forward.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I think I understand better where she is coming from in her second clarification.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Currently, we do have a Code for Fun programme.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We do work with agencies, such as CSA.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As I mentioned earlier in my response, we do touch on these topics through assembly talks.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We do touch on these topics through the Form Teacher Guidance Period for the younger ages, the lower primary ages.
